rejected_rule.statement: A document that is unambiguously a deed of sale cannot be construed by parol evidence to show it is actually a mortgage, but the true nature of the transaction can be ascertained through admissible extraneous evidence if there is ambiguity in the terms.
rejected_rule.supporting_quote: "It is never open to a party who executes a conveyance which is unambiguously a deed of sale to lead parol evidence to show that it is a deed of mortgage. ... Extraneous evidence can be adduced only if there is an ambiguity in the terms of the deed."
